analysis: The PR modifies only docs/developer/test.md. Changed ranges: the 'Last updated' date (line 3), a CI-routing sentence near head lines 1432-1433 that drops the carve-out where the 3 GPU shards ran on Blacksmith, and a CI-routing-test description near head lines 2056-2061 that adds a 'required' lane note and drops the 'Cluster GPU Tests on literal Blacksmith runners' claim. I examined the two supplied head_text units (lines 928-1806). The changed lines inside them are the 1432-1433 CI routing wording. The test-documentation text around them describes provider endpoint resumption, logout, add-on hold, native qualification, App Attest dispatch, SDK 27 qualification and the prefix-cache SSD tests. None of it changes executable code, a wire contract or a key-handling path, so it does not alter any provider trust boundary, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053..T-058), the add-on hold socket (TB-012, T-059, T-060), the privileged fan helper (TB-010) or the prefix-cache storage posture (T-041). It touches no cache TTL, key derivation or at-rest behaviour. The CI routing change is a documentation statement about GPU shards moving from Blacksmith to the routed job plane. I have no evidence of the actual workflow change, and the workflow and scripts are not in the supplied batch. Routing of CI jobs to different runners is a build-infrastructure matter outside the provider threat model. Release workflows are stated to stay on literal Blacksmith runners, which preserves the signing path. The remaining question for integration is whether the unseen .github/workflows or scripts changes match this text. That is a documentation-versus-implementation consistency question, not a demonstrated security regression. The patch excerpt for the second hunk is truncated, but the visible content is documentation only.
